Read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#responsibility-boundary) before using any image
from this project. This page is the support policy: which base and OpenSSL route
each series is built on, what it is pinned to, what the review record says about
it, and what the published names mean. A row being filled in does **not** mean
the version is secure, and it does not mean an image exists to pull. Why a pin
or a base was chosen is in `manifests/SECURITY-REVIEW.md` and
[manifests/OS-CVE-STATUS.md](manifests/OS-CVE-STATUS.md), and how a build or a
release run works is in [MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md).

How to read a row. `Debian base` is the OS the image is built on and `Base pin`
says whether that ref is pinned by digest -- a placeholder or an unpinned ref is
stated as it is, never rounded up to "pinned". `Source repo` is the source of
record the manifest points at, `Variants` what a release publishes for the
series, and `Composer` the release the image installs. `Patches` is the human
patchset decision (`PATCHSET_APPROVED=1` reads `approved`); a row reading
`pending review` is never built or published. `Security review` is the status
recorded in `manifests/SECURITY-REVIEW.md`: `tested-in-CI` means the image
passes the project's CI build and runtime checks, which is not an approval and
not a claim that a tag exists. Whether a tag exists is a registry fact, and
"Checking what the registry serves" below is how to read it.

## Upstream end of life

Every series above is end-of-life upstream: `php/php-src` stopped releasing for
these lines, which is why the source of record is a backports fork and not PHP
itself. The dates are php.net's own record (its unsupported-versions table plus
each series' changelog and news archive, read 2026-11-05) and they are closed
facts, so they are stored here rather than fetched at generation time.

| Series | Last official release | Released | Announced end of life | Pinned here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6 | `5.6.40` | 2019-01-10 | 2018-12-31 | `5.6.40` |
| 7.0 | `7.0.33` | 2018-12-06 | 2019-01-10 | `7.0.33` |
| 7.1 | `7.1.33` | 2019-10-24 | 2019-12-01 | `7.1.33` |
| 7.2 | `7.2.34` | 2020-10-01 | 2020-11-30 | `7.2.34` |
| 7.3 | `7.3.33` | 2021-11-18 | 2021-12-06 | `7.3.33` |
| 7.4 | `7.4.33` | 2022-11-03 | 2022-11-28 | `7.4.33` |
| 8.0 | `8.0.30` | 2023-08-03 | 2023-11-26 | `8.0.30` |
| 8.1 | `8.1.34` | 2025-12-18 | 2025-12-31 | `8.1.34` |

The release and EOL columns are not in order on every row, and that is what
php.net published: 5.6's end of life was announced on 2018-12-31 and `5.6.40`
arrived on 2019-01-10, while `7.0.33` came on 2018-12-06, before 7.0's announced
end of life on 2019-01-10, with nothing after it. "Pinned here" is this
repository's own `PHP_VERSION`, read from the manifest at generation time --
every series sits on php.net's final release today, and a row that stops saying
so means the pin is behind it.

## Composer

The Composer column is the release each image installs. Composer 2.x requires
PHP >= 7.2.5, so PHP 5.6/7.0/7.1 stay on the final 1.x release (1.10.28) and
7.2–8.1 ship 2.11.0. A manifest that overrides the policy pin without also
pinning a digest is labelled as unverified in its row. Where those two numbers
come from and how the built image verifies them is
[MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md#composer-trust-model); the digests themselves
are recorded in `/opt/php/BUILD-PROVENANCE` inside the image.

## Release tags

Published images are `ghcr.io/muffetlab/php`, and a release writes two names per
series and variant -- no third name, and no other registry:

- `ghcr.io/muffetlab/php:<minor>-<variant>` — the recommended deploy tag; it floats, and only within its own series
- `ghcr.io/muffetlab/php:<full-php-version>-r<revision>-<variant>` — the exact tag; `8.1.34-r1-fpm` is the first image built from PHP 8.1.34, `8.1.34-r2-fpm` the next build of it

There is no `latest` tag published for any variant: neither name above is one,
and `<minor>-<variant>` is the only name that moves -- it cannot change major
version. Choose the series from the table above.
[MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md#publishing-images) holds the rest of the model:
why no `latest` is published, what each of the four release inputs carries, and
how a run decides which series to build.

The release pipeline treats exact tags as immutable, so the highest revision the
registry serves for a PHP version is its newest image: a deployment that pinned
an exact name has to move to a newer revision -- or to `<minor>-<variant>` -- to
receive a fix.

## Checking what the registry serves

Which tags exist, and what each one resolves to, is the registry's answer, not
this page's. A release moves names and digests, so a table of them here would be
out of date the moment it earned its place, and a reader who needed the current
answer would be steered at a stale one. Read it where it lives:

- one name: `docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/muffetlab/php:8.1-fpm` prints the manifest list the tag resolves to, with each platform's digest
- the whole namespace: the package list for `ghcr.io/muffetlab/php` shows the tags the registry serves today

A name the registry does not serve answers "manifest unknown". A complete,
approved and reviewed manifest is a precondition for a release, not a claim that
one happened: a series is published by the release run that selects it. The two
names a release writes are the ones in "Release tags" above; anything else in
the namespace came from outside the pipeline, and
[MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md#publishing-images) says what a run is allowed to
write.

Each tag is a multi-arch manifest list covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`;
`docker pull` selects the matching platform automatically. There are no
architecture-suffixed tags.

The OpenSSL route is not part of a tag name either: one route is fixed per
series, so a suffix could express no choice a deployment makes. The
`OpenSSL route` column above is the answer, and the image carries it in
`/opt/php/BUILD-PROVENANCE` and the `dev.php-legacy.openssl-route` label.

Every claim on this page is about how a series is built, and every claim about a
built image is checkable in the image:
[DEPLOYING.md](DEPLOYING.md#checking-what-an-image-actually-contains) names the
files to read, and [MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md#publishing-images) records
what writes them and what is attested to the registry.
